correctness.rationale: For cactus cycles C_j each retained cycle is either entirely present and has zero bridges within C_j, or is incomplete and every retained cycle-edge is a bridge; noncycle original bridges remain bridges. Thus B=X−Σ c_j I_j with independent edge blocks, giving the exact joint PGF and Cov(X,B)=p(1−p)(m−Σ c_j²p^{c_j−1}). Strictly increasing Σ c_j²p^{c_j−1} gives the unique interior sign change iff Σ c_j²>m. Conditioning X=e makes the edge set a uniform e-subset: f(e)=e−Σ c_j(e)_c_j/(m)_c_j; its second difference is −Σ c_j²(c_j−1)(e)_(c_j−2)/(m)_c_j≤0, with correct endpoint first differences. Tree case, m≥1 and p=0,1 boundaries separately handled. Independent rational enumeration of triangle with 0,1,6,7 pendant edges at p=2/5 reproduced covariance exactly; the original source finite checker was inspected, not treated as an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Finite checks alone do not establish the all-cactus conclusion; the proof uses cactus block decomposition and conditional hypergeometric probabilities.

value.rationale: The exact bivariate law simultaneously determines arbitrary bridge-count mixed moments and the sharply characterized positive-to-negative covariance boundary across all finite cacti. Fixed-edge-budget concavity and at most two adjacent optimizers link Bernoulli and uniform-subset models. These are motivated structural and phase-boundary facts for a natural graph family, not merely a renamed known table or tiny unmotivated computation.
residual_risks: The factorization itself uses elementary independent blocks; value lies in the complete joint distribution, precise sign criterion and uniform-budget concavity, not in method complexity.

limitations: Common p∈(0,1), finite simple cactus with edge-disjoint cycles, m≥1; arbitrary overlapping-cycle graphs and heterogeneous p not covered. O best-of-knowledge subject to broader reliability-polynomial implicit coverage.
